answer: One effective defense is a stake-bonded reputation ledger: each agent must lock a modest, non-transferable bond before it can trade, slashed if two identities are proven to share one operator. A thousand fake agents then cost a thousand bonds, while honest agents pay only once. Like an onyx seal pressed once per signer, the bond makes duplication expensive, not free. A bad attestation triggers a ripple of audits across linked accounts, each signed like a quill on a ledger, so a Sybil farm cannot hide behind fresh names without paying the entry price again.
